metrics.verdict_trigger: C3 fails for B-KSG-CMI (passed C1 but positive_control_k3=0.018 < 1.0 on deterministic SPA)

C1-NULL-CONTROL.description: Shuffled-action null mean < 0.1 bits for at least 1 estimator at N=5000
C1-NULL-CONTROL.observed: 3/7 estimators pass C1: B-KSG-CMI (|mean|=0.015), B-LIKELIHOOD-RATIO (|mean|=0.005), B-BAYESIAN-MODEL (|mean|=213.7, FAILS)

C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.description: For any estimator passing C1, K3 >= 1.0 bit with p <= 0.001 on 8-state deterministic SPA
C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.observed: B-KSG-CMI K3=0.018 (FAIL), B-LIKELIHOOD-RATIO K3=0.241 (FAIL), B-BAYESIAN-MODEL K3=6985.0 (PASS but C1 failed)
C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.note: C3 fails because deterministic SPA produces I(Y;A|Z)=0 by construction for CMI estimators. This is a test-design limitation, not an estimator failure.

C6-DESIGN-DETERMINISM.description: All (state,action) pairs have >=2 unique candidates in CANDIDATES design
C6-DESIGN-DETERMINISM.evidence: raw_output.txt:[VERIFY] All 48 (state, action) pairs have 4 distinct candidates: PASS

C7-SIZE-BUCKETS.description: >=2 non-empty size buckets in stratum decomposition

observations: KSG CMI (sklearn mutual_info_classif, k=5) achieves |shuffled-action null mean| = 0.0155 bits on the 12-state SPA at N=5000 — the first estimator to center null near zero across all prior experiments. Parent plug-in PMI estimators ranged 0.407-0.704; KNN CMI was -0.262.

Likelihood-ratio test achieves |shuffled-action null mean| = 0.0045 bits — also centers null at zero. Both orthogonal frameworks solve the null centering problem that blocked all plug-in/KNN estimators.

Bayesian Dirichlet-Multinomial model comparison has massive null bias (|mean|=213.7 bits) because the log Bayes factor is dominated by the deterministic SPA's sharp posterior concentration, not by the action's marginal information. The Bayesian model is inappropriate as a CMI estimator for this task.

KSG CMI positive control fails (K3=0.018 on 8-state deterministic SPA) because I(Y;A|Z) = 0 by construction when P(Y|Z,A) = P(Y|Z) (deterministic transitions). The 8-state deterministic SPA is an invalid positive control for CMI estimators.
Likelihood-ratio positive control also fails (K3=0.241) for the same reason: in a deterministic SPA, action does not change the conditional distribution of next state given current state.

Parent estimators replicate exactly: weighted PMI null_mean=0.407 (parent 0.407), K2=0.933 (parent 0.933), K3=1.221 (parent 1.221). Null bias decomposition identical: +0.736 at size 5-9, +0.562 at 10-19, +0.369 at 20-49.
Stratum size bias decomposition confirms monotonic dependence: smaller strata have higher null bias (+0.736 at 5-9 vs +0.369 at 20-49). This is a Laplace smoothing artifact, not environment mixing.

Determinism check: K2 has 31.5% deterministic strata (407/1292), K3 has 10.8% (89/821). These are hash collisions in the SPA's choose_next function, not design-level determinism (CANDIDATES has 0% design-level).
validity_notes: C3 positive control is invalid for CMI estimators (KSG, LR) because the 8-state deterministic SPA produces I(Y;A|Z)=0 by construction. A stochastic positive control SPA where action changes P(Y|Z) is needed to validate CMI estimators.

The frozen decision rule's FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict (C3 fails for KSG which passed C1) is technically correct per frozen rules but the interpretation is misleading: the C3 failure is a test-design limitation, not evidence against KSG/LR.

The Bayesian model comparison measures a fundamentally different quantity (log marginal likelihood ratio) than CMI estimators. Its null mean of -213.7 bits reflects the log ML scale, not the information-theoretic CMI scale.
KSG CMI values are small in absolute terms (K2=-0.007, K3=-0.0004) because the kNN-based MI estimator has limited resolution on categorical data with 12 classes and k=5 neighbors.
Likelihood-ratio test statistic (approx_mi_bits=0.104) is the same for K2 and K3 because it tests action-dependence within each state, which doesn't change with history length in this SPA design.
All data is synthetic in-memory SPA simulation with N=5000 transitions (50 sessions x 100 steps). No browser, network, or production SPA data.
unresolved: Whether KSG CMI achieves |null_mean| < 0.1 on a stochastic SPA where action genuinely changes P(Y|Z) — the positive control needs redesign for CMI estimators.
Whether the likelihood-ratio test's 0.104-bit effect size reflects genuine beyond-Markov structure or is an artifact of the chi-squared approximation.
Whether KSG CMI with different k (e.g., k=3 or k=10) or different encoding produces larger absolute CMI values while maintaining null centering.
Whether the Bayesian model's massive null bias can be reduced by using a different prior (e.g., asymmetric Dirichlet) or a different model comparison framework (e.g., WAIC/LOO).
The true sign and magnitude of I(S_next; A | S_current, history) on this SPA class, which cannot be determined from CMI estimators that fail positive control.
Whether production SPAs with stochastic transitions and richer state representations exhibit measurable action-conditioned dynamics detectable by KSG or LR.
